meta.storyTitle: The Vibe issue ledger reflects reality, with evidence

summary.prose: This Story reconciles five open Vibe-integration issue records against the evidence this Epic's other Stories actually produce. It touches no application code: its only artifacts are the ISSUE records themselves, each updated with a specific, evidence-cited outcome -- closed with proof once its owning Story builds, reopened if a live check fails, or explicitly marked as deferred on the review rewrite rather than left as a stale open claim against machinery that no longer exists. This round also correctly files the HLD amendment for sc3's provenAgainst field (round 2's attempt used the wrong amendment type and was silently dropped by the applier; this round uses sharedContract.fieldRemove, verified against the applier's own code).

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: One shared plain-CLI Vibe execution adapter module owns the whole launch contract — argv construction, model/thinking pinning for new sessions with explicit resumed-session selection semantics (qualify or reject before dispatch, never silent substitution), prompt transport, budget guards, the execution context (cwd, environment, dual process-group policy with defined escalation and cleanup ownership per mode, abort signal, host deadline), the ordinary-session approval input with the existing chat mapping, rich turn events with session identity and tool-result output content, the qualified MCP tool naming split into general identity parsing and the analysis allowlist, and the fail-closed read-only mode whose qualification the ADAPTER owns and validates. The backend provider and the VS Code plugin chat both import and call it directly; the session-based app-server transport is deleted, not demoted. A sibling shared real-TOML config module (smol-toml, parse-for-understanding with surgical, byte-preserving edits) replaces every hand-written Vibe TOML reader. This is alternative a1, revised per the design reviews of 2026-11-24: the only shape that satisfies all seven Epic constraints, with k1/k2/k3 satisfied structurally — the safety gate, its qualification, the approval mapping, the process-group policy and the naming convention live inside the one module both surfaces must call.

consumedContracts.name: Adapter-owned read-only authorization and its qualification evidence
consumedContracts.purpose: The fail-closed read-only mode of the adapter: the qualification is ADAPTER-OWNED. provenAgainst's shape here reflects s2's own approved LLD (stableDescriptorHash, effectiveConfigFingerprint). This round files the HLD amendment (sharedContract.fieldRemove, verified against the applier's own code) that round 2's wrong-typed attempt failed to persist. The qualification evidence is what s6 cites when closing the read-only issue.

boundary.internal: The reconciliation work itself: verifying the chat prompt-transport fix, the approval parity cases, the tool-result output parity, the resume-selection behavior and the worker cleanup parity live with s3's evidence, checking catalog coverage, closing the implemented issues (read-only authorization via sc3's qualification evidence incl. its provenAgainst record, TOML parsing via sc4's story validation), stamping the review-dependent deferrals with their recorded dependency on the review rewrite, attaching evidence to every closure, and correctly filing the HLD amendment this round's own verification uncovered round 2 had failed to persist.

nonFunctional.durability: User configuration files are edited surgically with byte-for-byte preservation of unrelated content, and a config that cannot be changed safely is left untouched with the failure reported (k4); the issue ledger records closures only with evidence (k7).
nonFunctional.observability: Every turn result carries the tool's structured exit evidence and the session identity; per-turn outcomes, qualification results and refusal reasons are logged through the daemon's pino logger; the ledger reconciliation (s6) records its verification evidence on the artifacts it closes or defers.
nonFunctional.performance: One subprocess per turn, as the claude and codex clients already do.
nonFunctional.security: k1 is structural: the read-only launch mode is qualified live BY THE ADAPTER against the installed binary. All model access stays through the local CLI binary's own auth (k6) — no direct cloud REST.

dataModelChanges.entity: ISSUE-910fce32967bc4ea (Pass Vibe chat prompts correctly in programmatic mode)
dataModelChanges.details: Closed once s3 builds, citing s3's own TESTS record confirming all five live-verification cases (new turn, resumed turn, title generation, multiline prompt, option-like-text prompt) pass against the installed binary with no backend-path regression; reopened with the specific failing case recorded if any does not pass.

dataModelChanges.entity: ISSUE-d3e72fe73ee775a2 (Vibe's read-only session cannot call the insrc MCP analyze tools headlessly)
dataModelChanges.details: Closed once s2 builds, citing sc3's ReadOnlyCapability.provenAgainst record using s2's CURRENT field shape -- { stableDescriptorHash, effectiveConfigFingerprint } -- not the HLD's original, now-superseded { binaryVersion, effectivePolicy } shape. This is the evidence that the --agent approval gate this issue names is now correctly qualified rather than bypassed.

dataModelChanges.entity: ISSUE-0b3114f87754959b (Read Vibe configs with a real TOML parser)
dataModelChanges.details: Closed once s4 (sc4) builds, citing s4's own validation record confirming the real-TOML parse-for-understanding engine replaces the three named heuristics and handles the three reproduction cases correctly.

dataModelChanges.entity: ISSUE-738d62b848fd173f (Fix Claude on Ollama and Mistral Vibe streaming reviews) -- catalog-coverage sub-point only
dataModelChanges.details: The versioned-model catalog-coverage sub-point is annotated as resolved NOW, citing the catalog's current, already-shipped mistral-large-4 entry and this Epic's own live dispatch evidence (s5's approved LLD) proving --model mistral-large-4 runs successfully with all three declared efforts. This annotation does not wait on s5's own build.

dataModelChanges.entity: ISSUE-738d62b848fd173f (Fix Claude on Ollama and Mistral Vibe streaming reviews) -- Ollama/activity-review sub-point only
dataModelChanges.details: The Ollama activity-mode preflight defect and activity-mode review sub-point is annotated as DEFERRED, pending the review rewrite -- the activity-mode review machinery this sub-point depends on does not currently exist in src/. Annotated in place within the SAME record as the catalog-coverage sub-point above, not split into a separate issue.

dataModelChanges.entity: ISSUE-30962d0f44df1e76 (Support activity-supervised reviews through Mistral Vibe CLI)
dataModelChanges.details: Annotated as DEFERRED, pending the review rewrite, for the same reason: native Vibe activity-supervised review support is new capability work predicated on the activity-review protocol this Epic does not implement and the review rewrite has not yet re-established.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: This Story's reconciliation of ISSUE-d3e72fe73ee775a2 cites sc3's provenAgainst field using s2's OWN CURRENT shape -- { stableDescriptorHash, effectiveConfigFingerprint } -- as defined in s2's approved LLD (section 4.1). This Story files the missing HLD amendment (below), correctly typed this round, to close that sync gap formally.

invariantsToPreserve.text: A record closes only with the specific evidence that actually supports it.
A catalog-coverage concern already resolved by data present in the repo today must be recorded as fixed on that evidence now.
A record whose fix intent depends on review machinery that does not currently exist must carry an explicit deferred dependency on the review rewrite.
s6 cannot itself re-verify a fix live; every closure it records must cite the OWNING Story's own build/test evidence.
Reconciliation targets the specific evidence cited for each record, not a Story's overall build pass/fail status.

When a shared contract's HLD-documented shape and its owning Story's approved LLD shape diverge, a downstream consumer cites the owning Story's own artifact until the amendment that reconciles them is applied -- and an amendment proposal's acceptance into an LLD body is NOT itself proof it was validly filed; verify its shape against the applier's own code.

migration.stateBefore: Per this round's bundles: five open ISSUE records exist, each describing a Vibe-integration defect or capability gap, none yet carrying evidence-cited closure/defer annotations. Separately, s2's own approved LLD already amends sc3's provenAgainst shape from the HLD's original { binaryVersion, effectivePolicy } to { stableDescriptorHash, effectiveConfigFingerprint }, but round 2 of this Story's own attempt to raise this as a tracked HLD amendment used the wrong type (sharedContract.rename, which renames a contract's own display name, not a field inside its interfaceSketch) and was silently dropped by the orchestrator's dry-run against the applier (confirmed this round by direct re-read of src/workflow/amendments/applier.ts and orchestrator.ts) -- no AMD-* artifact exists on disk for this Epic despite that round's step having been accepted.
migration.stateAfter: Each of the five ISSUE records carries a specific, evidence-grounded annotation using CURRENT (not stale) field names. The HLD amendment for sc3's provenAgainst field is filed using the CORRECT type (sharedContract.fieldRemove, contractId sc3, fieldName provenAgainst, breaking:true, migrationCue naming the replacement shape and citing s2's LLD) -- verified this round against applyFieldRemove's actual requirements, so it is collected, dry-run successfully, and persisted as a tracked AMD-* artifact this time.

migrationSteps.action: Annotate ISSUE-738d62b848fd173f's catalog-coverage sub-point as resolved, citing the shipped mistral-large-4 entry and this Epic's live dispatch evidence.
Annotate ISSUE-738d62b848fd173f's Ollama/activity-review sub-point as deferred, citing the review rewrite as the explicit blocking dependency.
Annotate ISSUE-30962d0f44df1e76 as deferred, citing the review rewrite as the explicit blocking dependency.
Once s3 builds: annotate ISSUE-910fce32967bc4ea as closed, citing s3's own TESTS record's five prompt-transport cases -- or reopened, citing the specific failing case.
Once s2 builds: annotate ISSUE-d3e72fe73ee775a2 as closed, citing sc3's ReadOnlyCapability.provenAgainst record using s2's current field names.
Once s4 builds: annotate ISSUE-0b3114f87754959b as closed, citing s4's own validation record.

File the HLD amendment (sharedContract.fieldRemove on sc3's provenAgainst field, this round's corrected type) so the HLD document and s2's LLD no longer disagree -- superseding round 2's silently-dropped sharedContract.rename attempt.

migration.backwardCompat: This Story changes no application code, exported API, or shared contract directly -- only the prose content of five existing ISSUE.md records, plus filing one HLD amendment that formalizes a shape change s2's own LLD already made and s2's own (not yet built) code will rely on. Nothing consumes the ISSUE records as a machine-readable contract outside the insrc workflow's own ledger tooling. The HLD amendment itself is breaking (sc3's provenAgainst field is removed, with its replacement named in the migrationCue), but it only formalizes a change s2's approved LLD already carries -- no shipped BUILD ever used the old shape, so there is no runtime backward-compat break to manage.

alternativesConsidered.name: Evidence-cited annotation in place, with the amendment correctly filed this time
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Annotate each existing ISSUE.md in place with evidence-specific close/reopen/defer outcomes, citing s2's current (amended) sc3 field names, and raise the missing HLD amendment for that rename via the correct sharedContract.fieldRemove type.
alternativesConsidered.approach: No new tracked record is created. Each of the five existing standalone ISSUE.md files gets a targeted prose annotation naming the specific upstream evidence (Story build/test record or shipped catalog data) that closes, reopens, or defers it. For the read-only-session issue, the annotation cites sc3's ReadOnlyCapability.provenAgainst using s2's own current field names (stableDescriptorHash, effectiveConfigFingerprint). Because round 2's amendment attempt used the wrong type (sharedContract.rename, semantically a contract-name rename, not a field-shape change) and was silently dropped by the applier's dry-run, this round raises the CORRECT type (sharedContract.fieldRemove on sc3's provenAgainst field, with a migrationCue citing the replacement shape), verified this round against the applier's own code.
pros: Reuses the existing issue ledger exactly as designed -- no restructuring
Closes the amendment-tracking gap at its root with a type the applier actually accepts, confirmed by direct code read
Minimal footprint: touches only prose + one correctly-typed amendment proposal, no code
cons: Does not itself resolve the two OTHER ungoverned export asks (s3's buildArgv/readExitEvidence, s5's buildApprovalArgs) -- those remain openQuestions for the user to action separately, since s6 doesn't own that surface

alternativesConsidered.name: File a new tracked issue for the amendment gap instead of amending in place
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Open a new standalone ISSUE for 'HLD amendments proposed but never filed' rather than raising the sc3 amendment directly from this Story.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Rather than this Story proposing the HLD amendment itself, file a new ISSUE.md describing the general defect that amendment proposals from s2/s3/s5 were never tracked as AMD artifacts, and let a future triage cycle size and route the actual fix.
pros: Keeps s6's own boundary narrower -- it only reports, never proposes
cons: Adds a tracker-restructuring action this Story's boundary does not mandate (reconciling existing records, not creating new ones)
Delays the actual fix by a full triage cycle when s6 is already positioned, mid-design, to raise the one amendment its own acceptance criteria depend on (ac4)
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Punts the amendment to a future triage cycle instead of filing it correctly now, when s6 is already positioned to.

alternativesConsidered.name: Defer the catalog-coverage concern onto the review-rewrite dependency
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Fold the versioned-model catalog-coverage sub-point into the same review-rewrite deferral as the Ollama/activity-review sub-point, rather than closing it now.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Treat ISSUE-738d62b8...'s two sub-points as a single unit and defer both on the review-machinery dependency, skipping the independent catalog-coverage closure this round's evidence already supports.
pros: Simpler: one deferral reason instead of two differently-resolved sub-points in the same record
cons: Fails ac2 directly: the catalog-coverage concern is already resolved by data present in the repo today (the shipped mistral-large-4 entry) and this Epic's own live dispatch evidence -- deferring it on an unrelated dependency discards real, already-available evidence
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Fails ac2 directly: discards already-available closing evidence by folding it into an unrelated deferral.

alternativesConsidered.name: Close the review-dependent records wholesale instead of deferring them
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Mark ISSUE-30962d0f... and the Ollama/activity-review sub-point of ISSUE-738d62b8... as closed, treating this Epic's adapter work as sufficient.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Declare the two review-machinery-dependent records resolved on the strength of this Epic's adapter and TOML work, without naming the review-rewrite dependency explicitly.
pros: Fewer open records in the ledger
cons: Fails ac3 directly: neither record's actual fix intent (native activity-supervised review support; the Ollama activity-mode preflight) is implemented by anything this Epic ships, and the project's own steering confirms the review machinery they depend on was removed pending a rewrite -- closing them would describe resolved machinery that does not exist
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Fails ac3 directly: closes records whose fix intent is not implemented by anything this Epic ships.

openQuestions: Two other ungoverned pending export asks exist elsewhere in this Epic (s3's dependency on vibe-adapter.ts exporting buildArgv/readExitEvidence; s5's dependency on it exporting buildApprovalArgs) -- neither is owned by s6 or touched by this Story's boundary, and now that the correct amendment-filing mechanism (sharedContract.methodAdd for an export, verified this round against the applier's own types) is understood, the user should action those separately using the SAME verified mechanism.
